{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — E-Path FX / SFG License Agreement

**To:** Deal team  
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side)  
**Re:** Verified playbook findings and redline positions  
**Privileged & confidential — attorney work product**

---

## 1. Executive summary

We have completed a playbook review of the Agreement. The document is drafted almost entirely in the Licensor's favour, and in several respects it sits at or below our walk-away lines.

The three critical items are risk allocation, ownership and liability. Article XII is a one-way indemnity running solely to Licensor with extremely broad triggers, and Article XIII(a) affirmatively states that Licensor is not liable for claims that use of the Licensed Technology infringes third-party IP — combined with the "AS IS" disclaimer of non-infringement, we would bear 100% of third-party IP risk in technology we neither own nor control. Article XIII caps only Licensor's liability, at one half of amounts paid (below our six-month floor), while our own liability, including the broad indemnity, is uncapped and there are no carve-outs for confidentiality, data security, indemnity, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud or IP infringement. Article III vests all ownership in Licensor and, read with the broad "Derivative Work" definition and the customization work we commission and pay for under Article VII(b), sweeps deliverables we fund into Licensor's property; the Agreement is silent on ownership of our trading, order and client data.

The high-severity items concern exit and continuity. We are committed to a 36-month Initial Period renewable for seven years at Licensor's sole option, with no convenience right for us; Licensor may terminate immediately on any breach of any covenant with no materiality or cure; and Article XX(a) automatically terminates the Agreement and all of our licences on a Change of Control unless Licensor consents, with Licensor deemed reasonable in refusing whenever it merely believes its interests are affected. The licence itself does not extend to our Affiliates or contractors and cannot be transferred to a successor. Article XXI's Effect of Termination is one-way: we return everything within five days, with no Licensor obligation to return, export or delete our data and no transition assistance.

Favourable or compliant positions: governing law and venue (New York law, exclusive New York jurisdiction, no arbitration) match our preferred position; there are no liquidated damages, minimum purchase commitments or MFN/pricing-parity obligations binding us; audit cost allocation and the Article XXIII bar on termination damages cut in our favour.

Two findings — exclusivity and non-compete restrictions on the Customer — did not complete verification and require manual review before we send comments.

---

## 2. Findings

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Position / redline |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Missing | Confidential Information / Non-Solicitation (Art. XII; Art. XIII(a)) | Insert Licensor defence and indemnity for third-party IP infringement/misappropriation, breach of law, Licensor-caused unauthorised access to Licensee data, and gross negligence/wilful misconduct, with notice/control/cooperation mechanics and express carve-out from Article XIII; narrow our indemnity to Licensee-provided content and our breach of applicable law, third-party claims only. Fallback: IP-only indemnity with customary exclusions, procure-modify-replace-refund remedies and a 3x annual fees super-cap. |
| 2 | Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Deviation | § II License Grant and Restrictions I. (with Art. III, Art. VII(b), "Derivative Work" definition) | Add Licensee ownership of its data and of paid-for customization deliverables, with perpetual royalty-free licence-back for embedded Licensor IP and no joint ownership. Licensor's platform ownership preserved. |
| 3 | Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | Deviation | Confidential Information / Non-Solicitation (Art. XIII) | Make the consequential-damages exclusion and the cap mutual; reset cap to the greater of 12 months' fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000; add uncapped Excluded Claims; confirm fee obligations are not capped damages. |
| 4 | High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Deviation | General Provisions § (c); Art. XX(a) | Permit assignment to an Affiliate or M&A successor without consent; make other assignments (including any Licensor assignment) subject to reasonableness with no assignment to our competitors; remove automatic termination/consent right on our Change of Control. |
| 5 | High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Deviation | § II License Grant and Restrictions I. (with Art. IV, Art. XX) | Extend the grant to our Affiliates and contractors (we remain responsible for compliance), make it transferable to a successor in an M&A transaction, and limit revocation to uncured material breach. |
| 6 | High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Missing | § II License Grant and Restrictions I. (Art. IV; Art. XIX) | Insert a Licensee convenience right on 30 days' notice with pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; confirm Licensor has no reciprocal at-will right during the Initial Period. |
| 7 | High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity obligations binding Customer | **Needs review** | — | Automated review did not complete (tool loop exceeded). Manual review required before comments issue. |
| 8 | High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete restrictions on Customer | **Needs review** | — | Automated review did not complete (tool loop exceeded). Manual review required before comments issue. |
| 9 | High | LD — Liquidated damages / penalties payable by Customer | Compliant | Confidential Information / Non-Solicitation (Art. IV, V, XXI, XXIII) | No redline. Payment obligations are usage- or service-based; Article XXIII bars termination damages against either party. Audit cost-shift and the "Licensor" drafting slip in the payment floor are addressed under the audit and payment-terms rules. |
| 10 | Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Deviation | Art. II.IV(b) (fee tier schedule, "50+ US$5.00") | Cap audit frequency and add advance notice, business-hours, off-site/no-system-access and auditor confidentiality limits. Cost allocation already matches our preferred position. |
| 11 | Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Deviation | Confidential Information / Non-Solicitation (Art. X(b)) | Mutualize the non-solicit; limit to personnel directly involved in performance and to 12 months from the end of that involvement. Existing general-advertising carve-out retained. |
| 12 | Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | Deviation | § II License Grant and Restrictions I. (Art. IV.I) | Replace the unilateral seven-year Licensor-option extension with successive 12-month renewals by mutual written agreement and a CPI/3% cap on renewal fee increases. Fallback: automatic 12-month renewals with 60-day opt-out and 5% cap. |
| 13 | Medium | TRANSITION — Post-termination assistance and data return | Missing | Confidential Information / Non-Solicitation (Art. XXI) | Insert new Art. XXI(c): up to six months' transition assistance at then-current rates, return of Licensee Data in a commonly used machine-readable format within 30 days, then deletion and certification. Fallback: 90 days' assistance with the 30-day export retained. |
| 14 | Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Deviation | Warranty Disclaimer (Art. VIX) | Add an express warranty (professional and workmanlike services; 12-month software / 90-day services conformance to documentation; compliance with laws; no malicious code) with repair-replace-refund remedy, carved out of the "AS IS" disclaimer. |
| 15 | Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | General Provisions | No redline. New York internal law; exclusive jurisdiction of SDNY and New York state courts; no arbitration clause. |
| 16 | Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation obligations | Compliant | § II License Grant and Restrictions I. | No redline. No pricing-parity or best-terms obligation binds us; the only "other licensees" reference runs in our favour (Revisions made generally available). Right of First Refusal and Change of Control consent are addressed under the assignment/change-of-control rules. |
| 17 | Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum commitments / volume restrictions | Compliant | § II License Grant and Restrictions I. (Art. V) | No redline. Fees are usage-based per US$1m traded with no committed volume, minimum spend, take-or-pay or shortfall; the monthly support fee is consideration for services delivered. Term/exit concerns are captured under T4C and RENEWAL. |
| 18 | Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Missing | General Provisions | Insert new subsection (l) requiring CGL 1M/2M, E&O 2M, cyber 5M and workers' compensation, with certificates on request. |

---

## 3. Walk-away items

The following are at or beyond our walk-away lines and, on the verified findings, should be treated as conditions to signature rather than negotiating preferences:

1. **Third-party IP risk (INDEMN).** No Licensor indemnity anywhere, plus an express statement in Article XIII(a) that Licensor is not liable for infringement claims arising from use of the Licensed Technology, plus an "AS IS" disclaimer of non-infringement. This is the rule's walk-away scenario.
2. **Liability cap and mutuality (LOL-CAP).** A one-way cap at half of amounts paid is below our six-month floor, our liability is uncapped, and there are no Excluded Claims carve-outs.
3. **Change of control (ASSIGN).** Automatic termination of the Agreement and all licences on our Change of Control absent Licensor consent, with Licensor deemed reasonable in refusing, combined with a blanket bar on our assignment and no restriction on Licensor's — this combination sits at the walk-away line.
4. **No warranty (WARRANTY).** A pure "AS IS" disclaimer with no affirmative performance warranty and no remedy is the playbook walk-away position.
5. **Renewal (RENEWAL).** A seven-year extension imposed unilaterally at Licensor's option, with no notice window and no fee cap, falls in our walk-away zone and contradicts Article IV.II–III.
6. **Exit and data recovery (TRANSITION).** No right to recover our trading, order and client data from a hosted platform, and no continuity support, is below the walk-away line.
7. **Non-solicitation (NOSOLICIT).** Three years post-termination covering all Licensor and Affiliate employees exceeds our walk-away limits (no restriction beyond 24 months; none covering all Vendor personnel).
8. **Unlimited audits (AUDIT).** Audits with no frequency cap, no advance notice, no business-hours or off-site limit and no auditor confidentiality undertaking approach our walk-away position.

---

## 4. Next steps

1. **Clear the two open findings.** Complete manual review of the EXCLUSIVITY and NONCOMPETE rules, both of which failed verification (tool loop exceeded). We should not issue comments until we know whether the Agreement restricts our ability to use alternative FX trading technology.
2. **Issue the redline with the walk-away items grouped first.** Lead with the Licensor IP/misconduct indemnity, mutual liability cap and Excluded Claims, warranty, data ownership, change of control, renewal and transition assistance, so Licensor sees these as a single package rather than a list of preferences.
3. **Signal fallbacks selectively.** Where the playbook supplies one, we can offer it in the comment at first exchange: IP-only indemnity with customary exclusions and a 3x annual fees super-cap; automatic 12-month renewals with a 60-day opt-out and 5% cap; 90 days' transition assistance with the 30-day data export retained.
4. **Escalate the economics of exit internally.** A 36-month commitment with no convenience right, immediate Licensor termination on any breach without cure, and no data return obligation should be confirmed as acceptable by the business before we trade any of items 1–6 above.
5. **Flag drafting points for the working session.** The audit cost-shift mechanics and the reference to "Licensor" in the payment floor (identified under the LD review) should be raised under the audit and payment-terms rules rather than as damages issues.
6. **Confirm no change to compliant positions.** Governing law and venue, MFN, minimum commitments and liquidated damages require no redline; we should resist any Licensor-side amendment to the New York law and exclusive New York jurisdiction provisions."}
